interview.name: Dane
interview.answer: The repair drive is on Sunday at the community center.

reflections: Dane is helpful and practical, often stepping in with a simple plan and concrete support.
Gus responds with resource-sharing and encouragement, which lowers friction for the group.
Eli values structure and clear next steps, and becomes aligned once a simple plan is offered.
Dane is the main coordinator and prefers to keep the group moving with simple, actionable instructions.
Eli and Pia both want clear setup details before helping, especially timing and logistics, while Noah joins once the immediate task is clarified.
The group responds best when the plan is narrowed to a first priority, with safety and the smallest fixes framed as the starting point.
The group is coordinating a repair drive by breaking work into the smallest fixes first and assigning clear next actions.
Dane is taking an active hands-on role, repeatedly asking for the first small task and confirming immediate action.
Pia prefers written logistics and a concise prep list, while Ira is acting as a helpful updater who relays information from outside.
Dane is consistently positioned as a dependable helper who wants concrete, small tasks and follows through quickly.
Ira acts as a bridge for updates, keeping others informed while deferring action to the right person.
The group is coordinating a repair drive through incremental, clearly assigned fixes and shared ownership of updated details.
Dane is consistently responsive and willing to help with practical community tasks.
Mina, Rosa, and Oren are coordinating the repair drive updates and relying on Dane to help spread the latest details.
The group values clear, current logistics and simple task assignment for the repair drive.
